Well, it's March now and I'm looking at the year ahead. Twenty years I've been doing this — started when I was 25, took over from my father. I've got 58 mu here in Quzhou, four mouths to feed at home, and middle school is about as far as I got. The extension guy comes by sometimes, but mostly I go by what I've seen with my own eyes and what the neighbors are doing.

My land is split into three blocks. The biggest piece, 40 mu, goes to cotton — that's my cash crop. Cotton takes a lot of work and the picking is back-breaking, but the price has been steady around 2.9 yuan per jin and there's a subsidy, so it pays. Then I've got 15 mu where I do wheat-maize double cropping — wheat in winter, maize right after harvest in June. That rotation is my insurance. The wheat feeds the family and the maize brings in extra cash. The last 3 mu I keep for stevia — small plot, but it fetches 6.5 yuan per jin and the buyer comes right to the village, so no transport headache.

For the **cotton**, I plant letu variety around late March. I rotary till first, then put down basal compound fertilizer — about 100 jin per mu of general 15-15-15. The extension fellow says I could use more, but my neighbor does about the same and his cotton looks fine. I don't topdress much on cotton, the basal does most of the work. I'll irrigate twice from the well — once at flowering and once at boll setting. Pumping costs money so I don't overdo it. Pest control is the big job: I spray insecticide more than ten times through the season, herbicide once at the start, and I use growth regulator twice to keep the plants from getting too tall. I hire workers for pruning and for the picking in autumn — 40 mu is way too much for just family.

For **wheat**, it's already in the ground from last October. I used about 30 jin of seed per mu — saved most of it from the previous year, didn't have to buy. Before sowing I tilled with the rotary and put down urea as basal, about 35 jin per mu, plus 100 jin per mu of compound fertilizer. I'll topdress once more at jointing with urea. Irrigation is four times: winter irrigation, then at green-up, jointing, and grain filling. The well water is metered and every run costs me, but dry wheat is a disaster I can't afford. I spray insecticide three times, fungicide twice for rust, and herbicide once. I'm hoping for around 950 jin per mu if the spring rains cooperate.

For **summer maize**, the window is tight after wheat harvest in early June. I plant qiule368 hybrid seed — one package per mu, about 50 yuan. I do no-till planting straight into the wheat stubble to save time; by mid-June you can't afford to waste days. Basal is compound fertilizer, about 80 jin per mu of the special high-N type, and I topdress once with urea at the V6 stage. Two irrigations — one at jointing, one at tasseling. Insecticide twice, herbicide once, and a growth regulator once. If things go well I can get 1,050 jin per mu.

For **stevia**, I transplant chengguang variety in late March on that 3-mu plot. It's labor-heavy but the area is small. I put down 150 jin per mu of compound fertilizer plus ammonium nitrate as base, and topdress twice during summer. Five irrigations because stevia likes moisture. Pest control is intensive — insecticide and fungicide both eight times through the season because the leaves need to be clean for the processor. I do hand weeding too since it's only 3 mu. Expected yield is about 500 jin per mu.

Money is always tight. Fertilizer and hired labor for cotton are my two biggest costs. I could probably push harder on inputs, but I've seen what happens when you stretch too thin — one bad price year and you're in trouble. I'd rather apply a little extra fertilizer than risk a yield crash. The stevia plot is small but the returns are good per mu, so I keep it even though it's fussy. My wife and I do most of the work, with the kids helping during school breaks, but for cotton pruning, picking, and some harvest jobs I bring in hired hands. Total input costs this year will run me about 30,000 yuan. It's a lot, but I've got to spend money to make money.
